subject: Supplier invoice ingest: preferred channel + required fields sanity check
messages:
From: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@acmelogistics.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>
Cc: vendor-portal@acmelogistics.com
Date: Fri, 02 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Invoice submission for Redwood PO RWD-4721 — channel question

Hi Naomi,

We're getting set up to start billing against PO RWD-4721 for the July deployment work. Two quick questions so our accounts team can route invoices correctly:

1) Does Redwood prefer invoices submitted through your vendor portal (we see a link in the onboarding doc) or is email to billing@redwood.ai acceptable?
2) Is there a required invoice schema you need (line-level fields, PO stamp, tax id, GL code)? We're attaching a sample invoice and our export layout so you can tell us if anything's missing.

We can push invoices via SFTP/Drop folder too if that simplifies integration — happy to align.

Attachment: Acme_Sample_Invoice.xlsx (simple invoice export)

Thanks — Oliver
Oliver Grant
Finance Ops, Acme Logistics
oliver.grant@acmelogistics.com
(415) 555-0191

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@acmelogistics.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 05 Jul 2027 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Invoice submission for Redwood PO RWD-4721 — channel question

Hi Oliver — thanks for the sample. Short answer: we prefer invoices submitted via our Vendor Portal (https://vendors.redwood.ai) because it gives faster PO matching, automated PO stamping, and reduces manual steps in AP. That said, email is an allowed fallback for small volumes.

Minimum fields we need to auto-ingest (if you want invoices to land without manual work):
- Redwood PO number (PO-RWD-4721) on the invoice header
- Invoice number
- Invoice date
- Line-level description, quantity, unit price, line total
- Billing entity name + tax ID (for our tax team)
- Currency and total amount due

Optional but helpful: vendor GL mapping column, and a single CSV line per invoice with a field for the payment terms (e.g., Net 30).

Two routing notes:
- Portal uploads -> automated ingestion pipeline -> lower processing time (3–5 days to payment).
- Email -> manual triage for attachment parsing -> can add 5–10 business days.

We can accept SFTP if you want automated deliver; Marissa (cc'd) runs onboarding for SFTP integrations. Karthik can confirm required CSV column names if you want to send a sample export.

I'll attach a short field map and a minimal CSV template — please drop the sample invoice into the portal sandbox and we can validate.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Procurement Manager | Redwood Inference
aomi@redwood.ai
Attachment: redwood_invoice_field_map.csv

From: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@acmelogistics.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>
Cc: vendor-portal@acmelogistics.com
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 08:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Invoice submission for Redwood PO RWD-4721 — channel question

Naomi — thanks, this is helpful. A couple follow-ups after we tried the portal sandbox:

1) Portal upload validation flagged the "vendor GL mapping" column as unknown. Our AR system includes a chart_of_accounts_code field — is that what you mean by GL mapping?
2) We have bundled line-items for time-based billing (multiple service dates on one invoice). Will the portal accept grouped line items if each line includes the service date and a short description?

Also, for the fallback email flow, what is the preferred filename convention if we submit attachments to billing@redwood.ai? Our current pattern is ACME_INV_{invoice#}_{date}.pdf — would that work for your automated parser?

Attachment: Acme_Sample_Invoice.xlsx (updated with chart_of_accounts_code column)

Oliver

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@acmelogistics.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Invoice submission for Redwood PO RWD-4721 — channel question

Oliver — thanks for the sandbox test and updated sample. Quick answers and next steps: 

1) Yes: chart_of_accounts_code is exactly what we referenced as GL mapping. If you populate that column, our importer will surface a suggested GL bucket; finance will still review but it avoids manual lookups.

2) Grouped line items are fine as long as each line has a service_date (YYYY-MM-DD), description, qty, unit_price and line_total. We need explicit service dates for cost-allocation across sprints.

3) Email filename pattern ACME_INV_{invoice#}_{date}.pdf works for our parser. Please avoid spaces and include the PO number in the filename when possible (e.g., ACME_INV_12345_PO-RWD-4721_20270701.pdf).

Action items: 
- Oliver: drop one full invoice PDF into the portal sandbox and email a copy to billing@redwood.ai for us to validate the fallback path.
- Marissa: please confirm SFTP onboarding availability and provide the host + credentials checklist to Acme if they're ready to automate.
- Karthik: take the updated sample CSV and confirm the exact column headers (I think they should be: invoice_number, invoice_date, po_number, line_id, service_date, description, qty, unit_price, line_total, currency, chart_of_accounts_code, vendor_tax_id) — confirm and paste here so Acme can map.

Thanks — we'll aim to certify Acme for automated ingest this month once we get the sample.

Naomi Feldman
Procurement Manager | Redwood Inference
aomi@redwood.ai
(650) 555-0128
